rule: Ensure grouped sparklines have comparable start and end points and the same number of data points.
quote: generally this means that all sparklines in the group have comparable start and end points and the same number of data points.

rule: Keep titles and supporting text brief to provide context without overwhelming the visualization.
quote: Good titles and supporting text can be invaluable for providing context, but keep them as brief as possible.

rule: Include a data source citation to increase graphic credibility and allow deeper investigation.
quote: Providing a data source makes your graphic more reputable. It also allows those who are interested to dig deeper.

rule: Use visual data encoding to reduce user cognitive effort when processing multidimensional data.
quote: Visual data encoding was used to reduce user's cognitive effort, and filters were added to help customize views to user's needs.

rule: Add interactive filters to dashboards so users instantly customize views to match evolving analysis needs.
quote: Supporting interaction offered flexibility to instantly update data view to different inclusion/exclusion combinations as they came to user's mind.

rule: Design graphics with a data-ink ratio of 1.0, eliminating all non-data elements like frames and tick marks.
quote: Sparklines have a data-ink or data-pixel ratio = 1.0, consisting entirely of data, with no non-data at all. Thus sparklines have no frames, tic marks, and non-data paraphernalia.

rule: Design dashboards for a specific audience and context; align design with user needs, not all possible data.
quote: Discussions revealed challenges in balancing the amount of information shown, designing for a specific audience, and how to best contextualize the information shown.

rule: Use visualization styles that leverage human preattentive visual processing for fast and reliable data understanding.
quote: use visualization styles that work with human preattentive visual processing

rule: Use length and 2D position to communicate quantitative information quickly on dashboards.
quote: Visualizations should leverage human cognition and use length and 2D position to communicate quantitative information quickly.

rule: Stack primary actions first, then secondary actions as empty buttons in the actions array.
quote: Recommendation is to pass the primary action first and secondary actions as empty buttons

rule: Never hide title and value in metric charts; hide secondary elements like subtitles first when space is constrained.
quote: title and value will never be hidden

rule: Remove secondary elements below certain breakpoints to maximize space for primary elements like title and value.
quote: Below certain breakpoints, secondary elements such as subtitles are removed in order to leave as much space as possible for primary elements

rule: Use line charts for precise time-series analysis; use metric charts only for contextual trend information.
quote: If your goal is to precisely see the evolution of values over time please use a line chart instead

rule: Clarify filters and calculations in subtitles or unit text when metric values do not reflect the selected timeframe.
quote: If the values displayed are the result of any kind of filter and they do not reflect the current timeframe selected on your dashboard, please remember to make this explicit

rule: Translate error codes into plain language for users; avoid showing raw codes like '504' without explanation.
quote: Rather than just quoting the error code, we should translate what it means to the user in plain language.

rule: Use error pages for primary errors that block task completion and prevent showing the expected page.
quote: A primary error should redirect the user to an error page.

rule: Display error banners for secondary errors that block current tasks but allow the expected page to load.
quote: A secondary error should reload the page without the user losing any information, and display an error banner.

rule: Show error summaries and highlight affected form fields for validation errors without losing user input.
quote: Validation errors should reload the page without the user losing any information, display an error summary, and highlight any fields which caused errors.

rule: Avoid exclamation points in welcome messages; keep tone calm and welcoming to reduce user anxiety.
quote: Keep in mind that the user might be a bit nervous, so avoid exclamation points or other writing mechanics that make your tone sound excited.

rule: Empower users by stating what they can do, not what the product enables them to do.
quote: State what the user can do with the product instead of what the product enables them to do. This way, you give power to the user.

rule: Use icons with semantic color: gray for neutral states, red for errors, green for success.
quote: If you're not using a custom icon for a specific use case, an icon should be gray by default (except when it's used as a status icon).

rule: Use sentence case for capitalization; capitalize only the first letter and proper nouns.
quote: Use sentence case in your empty states: Capitalize only the first letter of the first word in the heading, body, buttons, or links.

rule: Avoid using 'please' in empty states; it sounds overly formal and is unnecessary.
quote: It's OK to use 'you' and 'your,' but never assign blame to the user. Also, avoid using 'please' in an empty state. It's extraneous and can make your message sound too formal.

rule: Use cards only for entry-level information; avoid cards for dense, repetitive, related content—use tables or data lists instead.
quote: Never use a card to show a dense amount of repetitive, related content. Use a data list or table view instead.

rule: Include meaningful images only; remove decorative images and ensure images help identify content types.
quote: Only include meaningful images on your cards (don't add them for decoration). Images should help users identify specific content types.

rule: Make card titles linked when cards are selectable or clickable to signal interaction.
quote: If a card will be utilized as a selectable and clickable card, the title needs to be made as a linked text to trigger action and indicate interaction.

rule: Use compact spacing (16px) as the default for cards; choose standard (24px) or large (32px) only for specific use cases.
quote: Compact (recommended): Compact cards use 16px spacing with an 8px spacer between the header and body, and a 16px spacer between the body and footer.

rule: Match skeleton structure exactly to the element being loaded.
quote: A skeleton should match the exact structure of the element you're loading in

rule: Use spinner when structure is unknown; use skeleton when structure is known.
quote: Do not show a skeleton when: You don't know what the structure of the component is going to look like.

rule: Combine filters between attribute categories with AND; within category with OR.
quote: Filters between attribute categories should be combined with a boolean AND operator. Filters within a category are shown grouped together and should be combined with a boolean OR operator.

rule: Show items satisfying more filters higher on page when otherwise unsorted.
quote: If the list is not otherwise sorted, items that satisfy a higher number of filters should be shown higher up the page.

rule: Add typeahead when dropdown list has large number of options.
quote: Use a typeahead filter when: A dropdown list has a large number of options. In these cases, typeahead can help a user find their desired option in less time.

rule: Use typeahead for single selects with more than ten items.
quote: typeahead is recommended for lists that are more than 10 items long.

rule: Show applied filter labels to reveal what conditions are being filtered on.
quote: Filter label: Shows users what conditions they are filtering on. Can show boolean relationships between different attribute-value pairs.

rule: Keep filter dropdown open as user selects multiple checkbox values.
quote: The dropdown should remain open as the user makes selections until they click away or manually close it.

rule: Set minimum width threshold for displaying all toolbar controls in data grid.
quote: minSizeForControls defines a minimum width for the grid to show all controls in its toolbar.

rule: Combine multiple preattentive features in visualization design to enable high-speed multivariate data analysis.
quote: These and perhaps other preattentive features can be used to create visualization tools which allow high-speed multivariate data analysis.

rule: Arrange elements along smooth, continuing lines rather than ragged ones to signal they belong together.
quote: The principle of continuity states, that we are inclined to interpretate visual objects as belonging together, if they are aligned on a smooth, continuing line rather than on a ragged one.

rule: Group filters and navigation elements close together; place view-specific filters near the views they control.
quote: Group global filters and navigation elements together. If a filter only applies to a single view, put it close to that view so the user understands that the two are related.

rule: Maintain consistent button styling across the dashboard so users recognize similar function.
quote: If your first button contains a white background with a blue stroke, maintain that style across all your buttons so the user recognizes that they have a similar function.

rule: Include a direct primary action button or link so users can act immediately.
quote: If there is an actionable next step, include a direct link in your message copy or a primary action button to make that action fast.

rule: Minimize content in empty states; more content carries a cognitive cost.
quote: More content doesn't necessarily mean it's a better solution as there is a cognitive cost for having more content on the page.

rule: Use centered images in small tiles to draw attention; left-align text and actions as a block.
quote: The centered image in a smaller space helps to draw attention to a state that may require user action.

rule: Use plain language in error empty states to help users diagnose and recover.
quote: Error messages should be expressed in plain language (no codes), precisely indicate the problem, and constructively suggest a solution.

rule: Allow users to safely explore and fail without stress to increase learning and confidence.
quote: When someone feels like she can explore an interface and not suffer dire consequences, she's likely to learn more—and feel more positive about it—than someone who doesn't explore.

rule: Always enable row hover state to help users visually scan columns.
quote: The data table's row hover state should always be enabled as it can help the user visually scan the columns of data in a row even if the row is not interactive.

rule: Keep column titles to one or two words; wrap to two lines then truncate, showing full text in tooltip.
quote: Column titles should stick to one or two words that describe the data in that column. In cases where a column title is too long, wrap the text to two lines and then truncate the rest of the text.

rule: Match toolbar height to data table row height for visual alignment and consistency.
quote: The toolbar height should always match the row height of the data table to maintain visual alignment and consistency.

rule: Use skeleton states instead of spinners for tables with expected load time.
quote: If extra load time is expected to display information, use skeleton states instead of spinners.

rule: Use zebra stripe alternating row colors to aid horizontal scanning.
quote: The data table can use a zebra stripes modifier to style the table rows with alternating colors to make scanning horizontal information easier for the user.

rule: Persist overflow menu icons by default; only hide on hover if visual clutter is a priority.
quote: By default, the overflow menu icons are persistent on each row. Having the overflow menus always visible signals to the user actions can be taken on the table rows.

rule: Disable single action icons and overflow menus when batch mode is active.
quote: When batch mode is active, single action icons and overflow menus on the row should be disabled.

rule: Use medium (40px) row height as default; adjust for density or readability needs.
quote: Use as the default and most commonly used size. Use when no specific density or spacing requirements exist.

rule: Review AI-generated summaries against source records before taking action.
quote: AI-generated summaries can be incomplete or incorrect. Review important details in the source record before acting on them.

rule: Limit empty state titles to five words to maintain clarity and focus.
quote: Try to limit to 5 words (not counting articles or prepositions).

rule: Use active verbs in empty state titles and descriptions to encourage user action.
quote: Title: A CTA that starts with an active verb. Description: A sentence that starts with an active verb and encourages the user to use a feature.

rule: Include analytics on all empty state solutions to measure adoption and improve over time.
quote: All empty state solutions should include usage analytics so you and your team can measure and improve the empty state solution you've created over time.

rule: Use one primary button per empty state context to emphasize the main action.
quote: If possible, use one primary button per context to emphasize the main action you'd like a user to take.

rule: Hide unnecessary UI elements in blank content empty states unless content is hidden but accessible.
quote: Hides unnecessary UI elements, unless there's content on the page that's hidden, but accessible through the UI (for example, archived content).

rule: Display a system-status message when no content exists to clarify whether loading is occurring, an error happened, or results are genuinely absent.
quote: Totally empty states cause confusion about how and whether the system is working.

rule: Never display misleading system-status messages that claim no content exists if the system is still loading; update the message when content arrives.
quote: Inaccurate system-status messages for empty states are particularly harmful.

rule: Provide direct links or buttons in empty states to start key tasks that would populate the container.
quote: Provide direct pathways (i.e., links) to getting started with key tasks related to populating the empty state.

rule: Show skeleton screens instead of spinners to reduce perceived loading time by 30% and bounce rate by 32%.
quote: A 2-second wait with a skeleton screen feels faster than a 1-second wait with a spinner.
finding: 32% bounce rate reduction with skeletons vs spinners; 47% more likely to wait for content

rule: Match skeleton dimensions exactly to content layout to prevent layout shifts and preserve visual stability.
quote: They maintain layout stability, prevent content jumps, and most importantly, they hack the user's perception of time.

rule: Delay skeleton display by 200ms for fast requests to avoid flickering; show minimum 500ms to ensure smooth transitions.
quote: Don't show skeleton immediately for fast requests

rule: Load and display content incrementally as available rather than waiting for all data, revealing sections sequentially.
quote: Load content progressively as it becomes available

rule: Reduce uncertainty anxiety by showing expected content structure in skeleton form before real data arrives.
quote: Prepares user for content structure

rule: Use CSS animations for skeletons instead of JavaScript to avoid layout thrashing and improve rendering performance.
quote: Use CSS for animations instead of JS

rule: Choose skeleton screens for full-page loads where content structure is predictable and helps set user expectations.
quote: A skeleton screen is used as a placeholder for a loading page. This progress indicator is used for full-page loads and reduces the perceived loading time.

rule: Apply metadata to all content items to support faceted navigation; single-dimension filters work only if they match user priorities.
quote: both existing and future content must have metadata applied for each facet

rule: Eliminate gridlines and unnecessary borders that do not contribute to viewer understanding of data.
quote: Eliminate gridlines and unnecessary borders that do not contribute to the viewer's understanding. Gridlines actually distract the viewer's attention from the actual data.

rule: Incorporate labels directly into visualizations instead of using separate legends when possible.
quote: Avoid unnecessary legends by incorporating labels directly into the visualization. For example, instead of an axis on a bar chart, we can have the values at the end of the bars.

rule: Reserve tooltips for specific, detailed information rather than displaying it on the main chart.
quote: For more specific information that you want to include in the chart, leave them to tooltips.

rule: Minimize background colors and shading to focus attention on the data itself.
quote: Minimize the use of background colors and shading to focus attention on the data.

rule: Avoid 3D effects in charts because they are difficult to understand and ineffective at conveying information.
quote: Be cautious with 3D effects, as these can be quite difficult for the average viewer to understand and are often not the best at conveying information.

rule: Prioritize primary metrics with most prominent visual treatment because they directly impact user experience or business outcomes.
quote: Primary metrics get the most prominent visual treatment because they directly impact user experience or business outcomes. System availability, response times, and error rates typically deserve top-level placement because they indicate immediate problems.

rule: Use color intentionally and consistently; red for problems, green for normal, yellow for warnings.
quote: Color usage should be intentional and consistent throughout your dashboards. Red universally indicates problems, green suggests normal operation, and yellow warns of potential issues.

rule: Avoid using color as the only way to convey information to prevent accessibility issues.
quote: Avoid using color as the only way to convey information, as this creates accessibility issues.

rule: Use line charts for trends over time, bar charts to compare quantities, and heat maps to show patterns across dimensions.
quote: Chart type selection affects how quickly people can extract insights from data. Line charts work well for trends over time, bar charts compare quantities effectively, and heat maps show patterns across multiple dimensions.

rule: Use white space and layout organization strategically to help viewers focus on important information.
quote: White space and layout organization help viewers focus on important information. Cluttered dashboards overwhelm users and hide critical information in visual noise.

rule: Provide baseline comparisons to help viewers understand whether current metric values are normal or problematic.
quote: Baseline comparisons help viewers understand whether current values are normal or problematic. Showing current CPU usage as 85% is less helpful than showing it's 40% higher than typical for this time of day.

rule: Use visual indicators or color changes to clearly mark when metrics enter warning or critical states.
quote: Threshold indicators clearly mark when metrics enter warning or critical states. Visual indicators like color changes or icons should make it obvious when values cross important thresholds.

rule: Provide drill-down capabilities to allow viewers to access detail without cluttering the main dashboard view.
quote: Drill-down capabilities allow viewers to get more detail without cluttering the main view. Dashboard hierarchies let users start with high-level overviews and dive deeper into specific areas that need attention.

rule: Design executive dashboards to emphasize business metrics and trends rather than technical details.
quote: Business metric emphasis shows how technical performance affects business outcomes. Revenue impact, customer satisfaction scores, and SLA compliance matter more to executives than server CPU usage.

rule: Include performance correlation displays to help technical teams understand relationships between different metrics.
quote: Performance correlation displays help technical teams understand relationships between different metrics. Memory usage correlated with response times or database performance linked to application errors help with root cause analysis.

rule: Update critical metrics every 10-30 seconds to catch problems quickly without overwhelming viewers.
quote: Critical metric streaming should update frequently enough to catch problems quickly but not so frequently that it overwhelms viewers. Error rates and availability metrics might update every 10-30 seconds, while CPU trends might update every minute.

rule: Batch non-critical metrics to update less frequently and reduce system load and visual noise.
quote: Non-critical metric batching reduces system load and visual noise. Historical trends, capacity metrics, and other non-urgent information can update less frequently without affecting operational effectiveness.

rule: Implement automatic reconnection for WebSocket connections so users don't need to manually refresh dashboards.
quote: Connection reliability mechanisms handle network interruptions and ensure dashboards reconnect automatically. Users shouldn't need to refresh dashboards manually when temporary connectivity issues occur.

rule: Use color-blind friendly palettes so status indicators remain distinguishable for people with color blindness.
quote: Color-blind friendly palettes use colors that remain distinguishable for people with different types of color blindness. Tools like ColorBrewer help choose accessible color schemes for data visualization.
finding: Approximately 8% of men and 0.5% of women have some form of color blindness

rule: Combine color with shapes, patterns, or text to convey status information accessibly.
quote: Multiple visual indicators combine color with shapes, patterns, or text to convey status information. Icons, text labels, and visual patterns ensure information remains accessible regardless of color perception.

rule: Ensure high contrast ratios between text and background colors for readability.
quote: Contrast optimization ensures text remains readable against background colors. High contrast ratios help users with various visual impairments read dashboard information clearly.

rule: Use semantic HTML and proper heading hierarchies so screen readers can navigate dashboards effectively.
quote: Semantic HTML structure provides screen readers with the information they need to navigate dashboards effectively. Proper heading hierarchies, labels, and landmarks help assistive technologies understand dashboard organization.

rule: Provide alt text descriptions for visualizations since screen readers cannot interpret graphs directly.
quote: Alt text for visualizations describes chart content in text form. Screen readers can't interpret graphs directly, so alternative text descriptions provide equivalent information for users who can't see visual elements.

rule: Support keyboard navigation with proper tab ordering so users who cannot use mice can interact with dashboards.
quote: Keyboard navigation support ensures that users who can't use mice can still navigate and interact with dashboard elements. Proper tab ordering and keyboard shortcuts improve accessibility.

rule: Adapt responsive layouts to remain usable on different screen sizes with appropriate information prioritization.
quote: Responsive layout adaptation ensures dashboards remain usable on different screen sizes. Mobile-friendly designs prioritize the most important information and organize it appropriately for smaller screens.

rule: Size and space touch-friendly interface elements appropriately for finger-based navigation.
quote: Touch-friendly interface elements accommodate finger-based navigation rather than precise mouse cursors. Buttons and interactive elements need appropriate sizing and spacing for touch interaction.

rule: Curate and simplify large complex datasets to provide overview of most important information at a glance.
quote: Dashboards offer a curated lens through which people view large and complex data sets at a glance. They combine visual representations and other graphical embellishments to provide layers of abstraction and simplification for numerous related data points, so that dashboard viewers get an overview of the most important or relevant information, in a time efficient way.

rule: Start empty-state headlines with a verb and use friendly, approachable tone.
quote: The headline should start with a verb. Use the friendly, approachable Trailhead voice and tone.

rule: Keep message line length under 66 characters per line in empty states.
quote: For readability, keep line length for each of these pieces under 66 characters per line.

rule: Make call-to-action text specific and answer what users should do next.
quote: CTAs are optional, but helpful. They should be as specific as possible, answering the question What should the user do next?

rule: Use illustrations in empty states only if they add clarity to the user's understanding.
quote: An illustration should clarify the situation. If your image doesn't add anything to the user's understanding, skip it.

rule: Create fewer dashboards with clear purposes and owners; adoption drops when too many dashboards are created.
quote: We've observed that the median workspace creates just two dashboards, and adoption drops off quickly beyond that. When every team spins up dozens, most go stale and stop being trusted.
finding: adoption drops quickly beyond two dashboards; most dashboards go stale when created in high numbers

rule: Match dashboard design to its specific purpose: strategy dashboards focus on long-term trends; operations dashboards surface wide metrics and highlight changes.
quote: Strategy dashboards work best when they focus on a handful of long-term trends that rarely change but help with alignment. Operations dashboards, by contrast, should surface a wider range of metrics, highlight unexpected changes and help teams react quickly.

rule: Tune dashboard detail and update frequency to audience: executives need less detail with annotations; daily/weekly viewers need denser, glanceable designs.
quote: Dashboards are most effective when their detail and update frequency are tuned to the audience. If a dashboard is reviewed only occasionally, it should include more guidance and annotations so it's easy to reorient after time away. If it's checked daily or weekly, it should be denser, more glanceable, and optimized for speed.

rule: Pair key metrics with context charts showing current, recent, and historical data to help users interpret performance instantly.
quote: One of the most effective dashboards I've seen pairs every key metric—revenue, conversions, refunds—with a simple chart showing this week, last week, and trailing highs and lows. Anyone, even without additional context, could instantly see if something was good, bad, or in line with expectations.

rule: Place the dashboard's most important view in the upper-left corner where users' eyes scan first.
quote: Most viewers scan web content starting at the top left of a web page. Once you know your dashboard's main purpose, be sure to place your most important view so that it occupies or spans the upper-left corner of your dashboard.

rule: Limit dashboards to two or three views to maintain visual clarity; create additional dashboards if scope grows beyond this.
quote: In general, it's a good idea to limit the number of views you include in your dashboard to two or three. If you add too many views, visual clarity and the big picture can get lost in the details.

rule: Enable highlighting between views so selections in one view highlight related data in other views.
quote: You can use the Highlight button on the toolbar to set up highlighting between views. When highlighting is turned on, a selection in one view will highlight related data in the other views.

rule: Limit custom styling of UI elements to maintain platform consistency and ensure accessible color contrast ratios.
quote: Custom styling of UI elements is intentionally limited. This is to maintain platform consistency with core UI elements and to ensure a high accessibility bar.

rule: Build app views with a ContextView as the default entry point to display content alongside Stripe pages side-by-side.
quote: ContextView allows apps to render next to Stripe content in a drawer, so users can look at them side-by-side and share context across your app and the Stripe content.

rule: Build apps for list pages only if features don't relate to a specific object; not every app needs a list-page view.
quote: Not every app needs to have a view for list pages. Only build for list pages if you have features to offer that don't relate to a specific object.

rule: Build apps for the home surface only if you can showcase relevant business overview material aligned with your product.
quote: Not every app needs to have a view for the home surface. Only build for home if you have relevant overview material to show incoming users.

rule: Use recommended UI component patterns to ensure high-quality, consistent user experience and faster app review.
quote: Using recommended patterns to build your app is the fastest way to make sure users have a high quality, consistent experience. It also speeds up the app review process.
